step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows data ingested from smart fire hydrant sensors into AWS API Gateway, stored in S3, processed in batch by Amazon ECS, and evaluated by Amazon SageMaker for leak probabilities. An analyst icon represents the human classification step.

graph.name: Mueller Water Products Intelligent Water Platform
graph.notes: Architecture for ingesting acoustic data from smart fire hydrants to detect water leaks.

nodes.name: Fire Hydrant Sensors
nodes.notes: Collects acoustic data from the pipe network.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Secure entry point for IoT acoustic data.

nodes.name: Amazon ECS
nodes.notes: Runs microservices to perform batch processing and signal correlation.

nodes.name: Amazon SageMaker
nodes.notes: ML endpoint that assigns leak probabilities to correlations.

nodes.name: Analyst
nodes.notes: Human analyst team classifying leak alerts.

edges.notes: Hydrant pushes acoustic data via API Gateway.
API Gateway persists data to S3.
ECS batch process ingests signal files from S3.
ECS sends persistent correlations to SageMaker for classification.
